title: Higher Yields And Corporate Profits
text:
Higher Yields And Corporate Profits

Tan Kai Xian

Gavekal Research | 22 Oct 2026

Equity investors were served a morsel of optimism Wednesday, as Meta’s chairman Mark Zuckerberg claimed the company’s AI investments “are paying off,” and raised guidance for total 2026 capital expenditure after third-quarter earnings beat estimates. Yet after a sharp sell-off in the shares of indebted AI names such as neocloud company CoreWeave, many investors remain jittery. They fear that with equity market performance powered heavily by the AI capex boom, higher yields will erode US corporate profits, triggering a broader sell-off. However, there are several good reasons to believe that the rise in yields so far is unlikely to inflict significant damage on US corporate profits.Add to personal dashboardInteractive chart
